name: MedHELM
intro: MedHELM提出了可扩展的医学任务评估框架，基于29名临床专家验证的分类体系，覆盖5大类、22个子类和121项任务。其35个基准由17个现有基准、5个重构基准和13个全新基准组成，其中13个全新基准里有12个基于EHR；框架以自动指标或三模型LLM评审团评分，并联合分析胜率与成本。
org: Stanford University, Stanford Health Care, Microsoft
build_method: JAMA任务起点, 临床专家调查验证, 现有与重构基准映射, EHR工作流任务构建
metric: Exact Match, Micro-F1, LLM Jury, Pairwise Win Rate, Macro Average
task_type: 选择题, 开放式问答, 分类, 生成, 对话
eval_feature: 任务专用提示与解析器, 公私混合数据, 三模型评审团, 成本分析
task_type_en: Multiple Choice, Open-ended QA, Classification, Generation, Dialogue
build_method_en: JAMA-task seed, clinician survey validation, existing and reformulated benchmark mapping, EHR workflow-task construction
eval_feature_en: Task-specific prompts and parsers, mixed public and private data, three-model jury, cost analysis
intro_en: MedHELM is a scalable medical-task evaluation framework built on a taxonomy validated by 29 clinicians and covering five categories, 22 subcategories, and 121 tasks. Its 35 benchmarks comprise 17 existing, five reformulated, and 13 new benchmarks, 12 of the 13 new benchmarks using EHR data. It scores tasks with automated metrics or a three-model LLM jury and jointly analyzes normalized win rate and cost.
metric_en: Exact Match, Micro-F1, LLM Jury, Pairwise Win Rate, Macro Average

drawio_review_note: Audited against arXiv:2505.23802v2, the paper's MedHELM v2.0.0 leaderboard, and the closest pre-v2 official source snapshot stanford-crfm/helm@2fcc2945005b9ae9f05d5dd382dabd3faa2de8f0. The bilingual diagrams preserve the JAMA-review task seed and clinician MK reorganization; the initial 5/21/98 hierarchy; the two-part survey of 29 practicing clinicians across 14 specialties and four institutions; 96.7% mapping agreement, 4.21/5 comprehensiveness, and 107 comments; the final 5/22/121 taxonomy; the 17 existing, five reformulated, and 13 new benchmark branches; 12 EHR-based new tasks; the exact 35-suite composition, 13-open/22-closed output split, and 14-public/7-gated/14-private access split; per-item context/prompt/task-specific-metric/optional-gold contracts; the gold-quality filtering experiment as sensitivity analysis rather than main-set deletion; the paper's exact nine models (DeepSeek R1, o3-mini 2025-01-31, Claude 3.7 20250219, Claude 3.5 20241022, GPT-4o 2024-05-13, Gemini 2.0 Flash, GPT-4o mini 2024-07-18, Llama 3.3 70B, and Gemini 1.5 Pro 001); benchmark-specific HELM prompts, parsers, and token limits at temperature zero on a PHI/HIPAA-compliant cluster; exact-match, Micro-F1, and open-ended jury routes, including NoteExtract's structure axis in place of completeness; temperature-zero, 4096-token jury calls with greedy brace-to-brace JSON extraction; the paper's ideal nine-score mean versus the source's successful-juror denominator (three int-cast axes per successful juror, with a failed juror dropping all three), invalid-JSON/missing-key/API-error juror drops, empty-candidate or zero-successful-juror default 0, and non-integer cast/truncation-or-failure boundary; clinician ICC validation; heterogeneous-score normalization uncertainty; paper versus source tie/missingness behavior; upper-bound pricing frozen 2025-05-12; Apache-2.0 code; and the non-release of 14 private datasets. Explicit boundaries note that the paper gives no 0-to-1 normalization formula, source code skips missing or non-orderable comparisons, the official leaderboard exposes original scores, the paper pins no repository commit or result checksum, and the latest site is a living release that has changed after the paper. Formal publication evidence [site-a11t-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2175×1433 (English) and 2173×1433 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2173×1431 and 2171×1431. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
